Subject: Function Overloading
Title: Promotion or Conversion
Notes: There were two different ways of transforming one type into another, promotion and conversion. Promotion is a special, pre-approved widening to int or to double; a conversion is any other change of type.

Subject: Function Overloading
Title: Small Types are not Promoted
Notes: bool, char, signed char, unsigned char, short, and unsigned short aren't in the ranking. They're promoted to int before any comparison happens, following the promotion table from before.

Subject: Function Overloading
Title: Conversion is any other type change
Notes: Promotions are always lossless. Conversions are not always lossy: some lose data and some don't. So "lossless" is true of every promotion, but it isn't what makes something a promotion. A promotion is simply one of the conversions on the fixed list from before. Everything else is a conversion, whether or not it loses data.

Subject: Function Overloading
Title: Why does this matter?
Notes: This matters because the computer may be faced with several different possibilities to transform the type. In that situation, promotion always outranks conversion. The computer will choose that first.

Subject: Function Overloading
Title: Default Arguments
Notes: Default arguments are not part of the function's signature. The function has the full parameter list, always. There is no promotion or conversion with default arguments because they must be the type specified in the function signature or the program won't compile.
